# Fixed read-only corroboration selector proposal

This is an English/data checkpoint for review, not an executable packet. It proposes one separately routed Python-only capture with a finite set of inputs. No source implementation, publication, dispatch, SDK, diagnostic tool, native image inspection by execution, managed target, namespace, solver or proof call is authorized by this document. The existing full diagnostic remains disabled. The original 44 harness files, including the original 19 lifecycle files, remain unchanged.

The selector contract is SELECTORS.json. SOURCE-REVIEW-LOCATIONS.json is a separate **private review aid**, containing local detached source paths. It must not be copied into public implementation or a runner receipt. It binds all 86 primary source files from the previously reviewed source manifest by byte count, SHA-256, Git blob hash, immutable upstream commit and URL. All 86 were independently rehashed locally as inert source data when this proposal was prepared. None was executed. The parent's nine-file detached critical review is referenced separately; its conclusions do not qualify source-to-installed-binary correspondence.

## Reference and meaning of a new capture

The historical reference is run 37254827562, commit bd478d28d0fbf307d4a1fbc817160dec0d0fab37, artifact 11322239172. Its ZIP SHA-256 is 3e9ca590a613a7c1f2e4f70d50b42526f65a96773b9eae7cbb749fa697fc7957; the candidate receipt is 7d396f12de57f0e034893a4a852d909615b43a29c7945e51b3247de73fdac9ec. That receipt catalogued 13,567 files. It was a successful bounded capture, not complete dynamic-load closure.

A future runner is a new input. Every selected path gets a current record and one of same-bytes, changed-new-input, absent-new-input, or not-archived-new-input. A path matching one archived pin is not a claim that the current runner matches all 13,567 files. Changed bytes, new aliases, a newly installed version, different package metadata or an unknown configuration include require a new reviewed input contract. They cannot inherit historical qualification.

All nine historical unresolved liblttng-ust.so.0 edges remain unresolved in this proposal, including the official runtime trace provider and the eight installed runtime trace providers. The four pending source contracts remain pending: runtime/hostfxr/framework/native ICU/OpenSSL/DAC; analyzer runtimeTargets/SOS/DAC; Python native extension selection; and SDK/compiler/task/reference-pack closure. No boolean in this packet can authorize a target or replace those contracts.

## Fixed sets and count arithmetic

SELECTORS.json enumerates each file spelling, record kind, presence rule, relevant primary-source IDs and any archived pin. Its expansion is finite before implementation:

| Set | Exact maximum | Intended evidence |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| SDK 8.0.425 text paths | 28 | `.version`; dotnet/MSBuild runtimeconfig and deps; fixed C# compiler deps; fixed SDK/common/NuGet targets and props |
| net8 reference-pack text | 3 | FrameworkList.xml, PlatformManifest.txt and PackageOverrides.txt under Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/8.0.31/data |
| Python inert text/config | 11 | exact sysconfig, Makefile/Setup/config sources and two importlib files |
| Public OS/config text | 17 | exact loader/NSS/hosts/resolver/OS/OpenSSL/CA/locale and inert Python site configuration |
| SDK static PE records | 11 | exact host/build/task/C# compiler assemblies; no Assembly.Load or custom attribute construction |
| Python hash/correspondence paths | 98 | deduplicated file paths from the archived 101 module associations, recorded without imports |
| Auxiliary paths | 4 | Python alias, ET_REL object, interpreter and ld.so.cache |
| Native alias probes | 77 | explicit loader/libdl/ICU/OpenSSL/NSS spellings; no recursive dependency discovery |
| Installed hostfxr images | 8 | exact versioned libhostfxr.so paths |
| Installed trace provider images | 8 | exact versioned trace provider paths, without optional-load waiver |
| Shallow directory observations | 6 | fixed immediate-directory name/count observations only |
| Official archive text | 5 | exact runtime version/deps/runtimeconfig and analyzer deps/runtimeconfig members |
| Package status selection | 32 names | only selected fields of matching amd64/all paragraphs from one bounded status file |
| Matching package-info text | at most 64 | at most one `.list` and one `.md5sums` alternative for each selected package |

There are 265 fixed filesystem file selectors; archive, status and directory selectors are separately counted. The maximum text reads are 28 + 3 + 11 + 17 + 5 + 64 = **128**. This counts optional absent files as potential reads and does not depend on deduplicating aliases. It is deliberately the full budget; implementation must not add another detached text source without a new selector review. Hash-only Python and PE observations are not permission to publish additional text.

The 32 package names are explicitly listed in JSON. The info alternatives are exactly `{package}.list`, `{package}:amd64.list`, `{package}.md5sums`, and `{package}:amd64.md5sums`, rooted at /var/lib/dpkg/info. For a package/suffix, at most one alternative may be present; two present alternatives are an ambiguity fault, not permission to read both and exceed the 64-read maximum. An absent package or info file is a recorded absence, not an instruction to invoke apt/dpkg, download packages or invent a substitute name. No Debian maintainer scripts, triggers, conffile bodies, or arbitrary package-owned files are opened.

## SDK, compiler and reference-pack capture

The fixed SDK root is /usr/share/dotnet/sdk/8.0.425. The reference-pack root is /usr/share/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/8.0.31. No latest-version resolution is executed. The only immediate SDK names eligible for presence observations are 8.0.131, 8.0.206, 8.0.319 and 8.0.425, with a 64-entry root limit. A new name is represented by bounded count/name digest and a new-input marker; it does not expand the roots.

The `.version` bytes and compiler/MSBuild assembly identity/informational-version strings may identify source ownership candidates. They are producer declarations, not verified source/build provenance. Read PE/CLI headers and bounded metadata tables as bytes only. The required facts are full assembly identity, MVID, all bounded AssemblyRef rows and the three named string attributes in JSON. Never execute attribute constructors, a resolver, csc, MSBuild or an SDK task. Unsupported/malformed metadata produces a fault and preserves the file pin; it cannot be replaced by runtime reflection.

JSON deps/runtimeconfig files are inert records. Capture framework identity, roll-forward/globalization settings, libraries/targets and native/runtime/runtimeTargets entries within the stated bounds. An unlisted dependency remains a recorded uninspected dependency. XML imports, UsingTask locations, KnownFrameworkReference entries, reference-pack file rows and properties are inert records; never expand MSBuild properties, evaluate conditions, import targets, resolve SDKs or open a path because an XML node named it. Reject DOCTYPE/entity forms before parsing, with no external entity/network handling. A new imported file/task/refpack path needs a separately reviewed selector.

The pinned SDK ProcessFrameworkReferences and framework-resolution targets explain why targeting-pack availability and package acquisition need review; they do not prove current task selection. This packet does not choose workloads, acquire missing packs, enumerate every compiler dependency or qualify an SDK build. Roslyn/MSBuild/NuGet source versions, distribution patches and actual selections remain pending until metadata supplies precise ownership candidates and a later source audit resolves them.

## Python files and interpreter boundaries

The 101 archived module-to-file associations are preserved literally. They deduplicate to 98 fixed file paths; no stdlib/site-packages tree walk is allowed. Some associations describe frozen modules whose `__file__` points at a source file: pinning that source does not prove it supplied the running frozen module body. The two bootstrap source files and sysconfig/build records are read as inert text. Do not evaluate sysconfig Python assignments, execute python-config, import sitecustomize, evaluate Makefile expressions, load python.o, or choose a pyc body.

The Python3.12 `python.o` remains ET_REL/header-only outside the load graph. Upstream v3.12.3 source provides import/dlopen algorithms but not correspondence to Ubuntu's compiled and patched Python. The interpreter file, package Source/Version declarations, inert build/config text and selected module files are corroboration facts only. A matching `.list`/`.md5sums` entry is installed-package ownership, not authenticity or source-build equality.

The future packet's sole execution is the isolated Python host itself. It must have a separately reviewed fixed source/import set, no user/site imports and no cached body replacing a hash-checked packet source. Necessary interpreter startup and ordinary declared stdlib imports are interpreter execution and must be reported honestly; this proposal does not call those native extension loads source-closed. “No native loader bodies” means no use of CDLL/dlopen/Assembly.Load, or target/native-image execution to inspect an eligible image. A native target cannot be loaded to make metadata parsing convenient. Final imported modules and mapped files may be observed from the running host only through a later explicitly reviewed in-process receipt extension; there is no implicit `/proc` tree traversal in these selectors.

## Loader, ICU, OpenSSL and NSS metadata

Native alias paths are explicit in JSON. Their source is the observed glibc/merged-usr layout, pinned .NET ICU/OpenSSL lookup code and ClrMD's libdl fallback. The list covers loader/libc/libdl/libm/compiler-support/libffi, the versioned OpenSSL alternatives named by the shim, ICU unversioned/70/70.1/74/74.2 spellings, five NSS module names and three exact legacy-provider locations. Unsupported or missing alternatives are evidence, never newly loaded candidates.

Capture regular-file identity, bounded symlink chain, ELF identification/type/machine/version/header facts and only the bounded dynamic entries PT_INTERP, DT_NEEDED, DT_SONAME, DT_RPATH and DT_RUNPATH. No symbol/export enumeration is needed for this corroboration packet. There is no ldd/readelf/native-loader call, no graph walk to open newly named dependencies and no disassembler. The ELF-eligible set is only these exact aliases, eight hostfxr paths, eight trace-provider paths, and the explicitly typed interpreter/object auxiliary records. ELF ET_REL remains separate. Unknown/reserved/core/none or malformed loadable headers remain blockers; this proposal cannot reuse the old ET_REL repair to weaken ET_EXEC/ET_DYN validation.

Alias resolution has at most eight hops. A content read may end only at another exact selector or an explicitly enumerated archived resolved endpoint. Unknown endpoints are not opened. Record the source alias's pin and a safe unknown-target fault, not the bytes of an arbitrary symlink destination. Config aliases have their own exact endpoint list. Absence is an ENOENT/ENOTDIR record for an exact spelling with readable parent identity before/after. Permission denial, an unknown endpoint, a changed parent or other errors are not absence. Even stable absence at all listed aliases is not global loader-search absence.

The shallow observations are only the declared SDK/fxr roots, ld.so.conf.d, two ossl-modules roots and openssl.cnf.d. Each has an exact eligible immediate-name set and a 32-entry maximum except SDK's 64. No descendants of an unknown entry are opened. Unknown names themselves need not be published: publish total count and a bounded sorted-name digest, keeping the selected known-name observations. The directory may change during inspection; record that rather than treating it as a frozen namespace. /etc/ssl/private and other prohibited roots are never listed.

Loader cache/config parsing is inert. Unknown ld.so.conf includes/search directories are recorded without scanning them. NSS captures the public service/rule configuration and selected provider files, without issuing resolver/account queries or opening passwd/group/shadow. OpenSSL captures only the fixed public config/CA paths and exact legacy module metadata. Unknown includes, expanded environment variables, engine/provider names, file references, keyfiles and module locations are not followed. Config text is a prerequisite to reviewing provider/config semantics, not proof that Python/OpenSSL/.NET will or will not load another module.

The .NET shim source is not the OS OpenSSL provider or glibc NSS implementation. Matching dpkg Source/version records can identify the specific upstream plus Ubuntu patch source to fetch for a later independent audit. This packet deliberately does not fetch source archives, installed headers or native exports. Those are separate research/capture scopes once exact ownership is known. ICU library presence does not prove all required versioned dlsym symbols are present. The future ICU ABI/export audit must name its precise symbol set and source macros before implementation.

## Public-content and secret boundary

Only the 17 named public config/text paths and the fixed SDK/Python/archive data may be detached. The public CA bundle is the single explicitly allowed certificate payload. Config references grant no authority to read referenced files. No credentials, authentication state, private keys, home directories, proc environ, sudo/SSH/cloud state, shadow/gshadow, passwd/group, secret directories or package scripts are read. A private-looking reference is not printed verbatim in a fault. Private-key content markers and credential/password/token/auth assignments in an otherwise eligible text prevent publication of that text; publish only its bounded byte count/hash and a safe rejection code. The later implementation must review its precise conservative detector before it is runnable.

Package metadata contains no authority to follow its full file list. Detach selected status fields and only `.list`/`.md5sums` records whose paths match the requested/resolved selector set. Omit forbidden entries with a count/digest. Do not read arbitrary installed package files. All before/after/hash facts remain accurate even if text publication is withheld; withholding means the corroboration content is incomplete, not passed source closure.

## Record and fault contract

SELECTORS.json names the required fields and enums for FileObservation, TextObservation, PackageObservation, ELFObservation, PEObservation, DirectoryObservation and PacketSummary. Future implementation must reject omitted/unknown acceptance-critical fields, non-boolean booleans, duplicate selector IDs/records and uncontrolled path expansion. Detached parsed references retain their owner selector and source-byte pin. There is no caller-supplied approval field.

Raw /var/lib/dpkg/status processing is capped at 16 MiB and 512 selected paragraphs. The 32 selected names have only amd64/all architecture eligibility. Parse bounded RFC822-like fields as data, preserve each selected raw paragraph SHA, and detach only Package, Status, Version, Architecture, Source, Depends, Pre-Depends, Built-Using and Essential. Unknown package paragraphs are not detached, do not expand the names and do not authorize an ownership guess. Duplicate selected package identities and competing owners are explicit ambiguity faults. The actual package status/Source fields are new runner inputs.

Every potential text read is at most 4 MiB, and all text-read bytes together at most 64 MiB. The 128 limit covers source raw text used by parsers even if it is eventually not published. Hash-only records use the inherited 512 MiB/file and 8 GiB aggregate ceilings. Dynamic ELF entries are at most 8,192/image; needed names and PE assembly refs at most 256/image; symlink-resolved images at most 128; each package-info file at most 65,536 records; report at most 32 MiB. JSON has bounded nesting/member counts; no pickle, marshal, eval or Python import accepts data. Counts reaching a cap produce a fault before another record/body is consumed.

Work has the inherited 600-second deadline, followed by independent 30-second finalization and five-second publication bounds. Retain the first fault. Finalization cannot overwrite a work fault with a later deadline/error or claim success if capture was partial. Record source/selector/known archived input pins before and after, plus bounded rechecks of selected current files/directories. A complete future capture means every required data observation was obtained within those bounds. It still requires completeDynamicLoadClosure=false, reviewedRunnerClosure=false, fullDiagnosticEnabled=false, SDKExecuted=false, collectorExecuted=false, analyzerExecuted=false and targetExecuted=false.

## Source reuse and next review boundary

The original inventory.py is preserved byte-identically at SHA-256 01b1522c9405f95f82c6da1f56ff7185d5b83c2b80c7732b8a52accd83664d1b. It is neither invoked nor imported by this proposed narrow route: calling it would repeat broader archive/tree capture rather than the declared selector scope. Its existing file, manifest and historical results stay intact. A future separately named packet implementation would be reviewed as new source, with a distinct manifest/workflow/outer coordinator and pinned source-byte startup guard. Shared data pins do not imply unchanged executable parser code.

The immediately reviewable output here is the exact selector/record contract plus local primary-source locations. After approval, implement and freeze only that fixed corroboration route, then obtain one actual packet and independently inspect its data. Only then identify the exact OS/package/SDK source owners and propose a complete typed closure/confinement contract. No complete hostfxr, transient failed-load, DAC/SOS, ICU, OpenSSL provider/NSS, namespace or GC-root claim can precede that work.

The nine tracing edges remain unresolved. The constructor's attempted sibling dlopen and ignored failure are not suppressed by EnableEventLog=0; any future optional failed-load contract is distinct from archive availability. The managed runtime's 2 TiB sparse JIT double mapping remains relevant to finite RLIMIT_FSIZE; this packet provides no cap safety proof. Analyzer LoadExtensions occurs before opening the dump and symbol stores are enabled before the first command; future lazy-import/command resolution and confinement must precede acceptance. `gcroot`'s current managed Option attributes omit `-all` even though help text mentions it; default output uses PrintAllRoots but is not a claim that all possible reference paths are enumerated. No real GC root has been observed, and the failed six-smoke remains failed.
